chunk_map.heading: What good means is yours to write
A check is what good means, written down
Criteria keep a floor and can raise a ceiling
A pass is a claim about a check nobody has tested

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 1 line 8 (slides/write-down-what-good-means.md): "Hold your overnight digest against those lines" is the closest; the digest is the training spine artifact earned earlier in the same module family (whats-actually-true.md lists Exercise: Read the digest, Lecture: The digest is back before this lecture in learn-faster-than-the-market) so arc-earned carve-out applies, and "those lines" resolves to the three criteria in the preceding paragraph. chunk 2 "both grounded" resolves to "two opportunity summaries".
Closest: chunk 1 "your overnight digest" names the artifact by name, not by position ("the earlier lecture"). No "the opening lecture/previous module" phrasing in any of the four slides.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Only backward reference is "your overnight digest" (write-down-what-good-means.md:8). Beat exists: curriculum/trainings/agentic-product-teams-101/whats-actually-true.md lines 24-26 include Exercise: Read the digest and Lecture: The digest is back; learn-faster-than-the-market.md:29-31 places this lecture after them.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no guess-before-reveal or live-demo beat; four declarative slides

rules_evaluated.evidence: Smallest chunk is the-floor-and-the-ceiling (4 short paragraphs) and a-pass-is-a-claim; each carries its own claim ("A pass ... means it saw nothing wrong. It does not mean the work is good", a-pass-is-a-claim.md:4). No wait-state chunk.

Closest: chunk 2 header "Criteria keep a floor and can raise a ceiling" over a body that defines floor (para 1) and ceiling (paras 2-3), line 10 restates both. Chunk 3 "A pass is a claim about a check nobody has tested" matches line 4 "Until you compare the check's verdicts with your own, you do not know". No header contradicted.

Closest: the-floor-and-the-ceiling.md:4 "Every customer quote traces to an interview. Every number traces to its report. Every claim points to evidence or says what is missing." is an anaphora triple, but the third leg adds new content (the missing-evidence case) and changes the verb, so it clears the third-leg test. Sub-items: no "Not X. Not Y. Z." (grep of "Not " sentences: none), no self-grading superlative, no number+retraction (Husain figure scoped "on one product", a-pass-is-a-claim.md:6), no abstraction-noun stack, no verb triplet.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: "check" (one meaning throughout) and "the floor/ceiling" are plain product-register words; maintainer STATUS notes say no eval/judge/gate vocabulary and body grep finds none of: eval, judge, rubric, gate in slide bodies except header slug names in comment anchors (not rendered). View greps banned_words CLEAN (0).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -c "\*\*" over slide bodies above <!-- maintainer --> -> 0 on all four slides (the counts of 2/2/5/5 per file are all maintainer/backing-block bold). Zero bold is inside the ≤1 budget.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Lecture is included by learn-faster-than-the-market.md:31 as "[Lecture: What good means is yours to write](lectures/apt101-what-good-means.md)" and each of the four slides is an include link at lectures/apt101-what-good-means.md:3-9 resolving to an existing curriculum/slides file (ls confirmed all four).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js --file curriculum/lectures/apt101-what-good-means.md -> "OK — 1 files, Phase/Step numbering consistent." No hand-numbered headers.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --file curriculum/lectures/apt101-what-good-means.md -> "OK — 1 files, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut."

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no in-body links; only structural include links, explicitly out of scope; rule states no standing requirement

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/slides/<each of the 4 slides> -> "oversized: 0 ... every slide is within limits" for write-down-what-good-means, the-floor-and-the-ceiling, a-pass-is-a-claim, your-rubric-becomes-a-target.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Lecture headings are all claims: "A check is what good means, written down", "Criteria keep a floor and can raise a ceiling", "A pass is a claim about a check nobody has tested", "Your criteria become a target". None is a bare label.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: the-floor-and-the-ceiling.md:10 "The floor keeps the work tied to its sources. The ceiling makes it worth reading." is a closing line that nearly restates the header (class c), but it introduces "worth reading" as the ceiling test, which paragraphs 2-3 only imply, so it adds a handle; offered as a suggestion, no gate. No doctrine restatement or pedagogy commentary elsewhere.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A retitled slide re-earns its bullets against the new header.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Covered each header and read its body: write-down-what-good-means (body = example criteria then written-down standard), the-floor-and-the-ceiling (floor, ceiling, written-down difference), a-pass-is-a-claim (pass vs check, calibrate, Husain), your-rubric-becomes-a-target (Goodhart, factory, one human question). Every paragraph answers its current header; no inherited bullets from an older header. Closest: the-floor-and-the-ceiling.md:4 final "It can still be useless." sets up the ceiling, so it serves the current header.

suggestions.now: The floor keeps the work tied to its sources. The ceiling makes it worth reading.
suggestions.proposed: (cut; slide ends on "Write it down, and it becomes criteria the agents can aim at.")
